headings.title: Mobile task submission and queue sheets

html:
Mobile task submission and queue sheets

The dedicated mobile shell captures task intent and observes the same server-owned conversation lanes as desktop. Its composer and queue sheet have their own lifetimes. This guide follows those boundaries; the conversation coordinator remains the authority for task admission, retry identity, dependencies and execution.

The browser queue guide explains desktop submission, the common dependency-selection contract and the shared continuation panel. Mobile Run After selection uses a separate entry point with that same contract. Queued continuations and live steering use the shared instruction editor and lineage queue; they are distinct from the conversation queue sheet described here.

Data and component ownership

Implementation Responsibility
mobile/submission_options.js Synchronously captures loaded composer/target intent and policy overrides before asynchronous submission.
mobile/task_dependencies.js Keeps an explicit task dependency scoped to the current conversation, projects candidates and restores failed-submission intent only if it remains current.
mobile/app.js Combines prompt/resources/options, tracks pending submission identities, checks agreement and navigation, consumes accepted drafts and applies canonical snapshots.
mobile/lazy/queue.js Opens queue rows, sends explicit mutations and updates existing dependency/start controls through the shell's invalidation owner.
mobile/api.js Supplies page state, safe text nodes, per-button action ownership, same-origin JSON transport and scoped draft consumption.
mobile/overlays.js Owns the single sheet, replacement/close callbacks, modal focus and browser-history entry.
flowchart TD Text[Exact composer text] --> Body[Captured submission body] Resource[Attachment and resource-editor IDs] --> Body Dependency[Scoped Run After identity] --> Body Profile[Loaded composer profile and selected controls] --> Options[Synchronous submissionOptions] Targets[Loaded target registry and draft selection] --> Options Checks[Agent Checks and runtime guard overrides] --> Options Options --> Body Body --> Identity[Page-local exact-body key and retry ID] Identity --> Gate[Agreement and navigation checks] Gate --> API[Server task and lane APIs] API --> Accepted[Accepted task identity] Accepted --> Draft[Consume matching submitted draft and selected resources] Accepted --> Read[Canonical conversation snapshot owner] Read --> Views[Task cards, composer and queue summary] Read --> Sheet[Mounted queue dependency and Start controls] Sheet --> Action[Explicit task or lane mutation] Action --> API

submissionOptions requires the composer profile to be ready, no current composer problem, and an available draft target. It returns the profile's submission fields, current target group and primary target labels, selected mode/effort, permission/capability intent, runtime guards and Agent Checks overrides. It makes no API call and starts no work. Labels/locality are presentation data; server admission and preflight validate current execution authority.

Null permission or capability choices retain inheritance. The function reads already-loaded state; it does not refresh policy or target authority during capture. The caller adds exact prompt text, conversation/dependency identity and deduplicated attachment IDs. Resource-editor Gateway IDs extend the captured target group while retaining its primary Gateway.

Submission and retry sequence

The mobile submit path waits for composer resources, then captures text, conversation, navigation generation and dependency revision. Blank text, another submission, resource loading, page loading and pending interactions prevent a new send. For ordinary conversation tasks it builds the complete body synchronously and finds or creates a retry ID keyed by that body's serialized JSON.

sequenceDiagram participant U as Mobile composer participant S as Submission owner participant D as Dependency and draft owners participant L as Loaded views and agreement gate participant A as Conversation task API U->>S: Submit exact text and current selected intent S->>S: Capture body, generation and pending retry identity S->>L: Ensure view module and accepted agreement alt Gate declines or navigation changed L-->>S: Do not proceed S-->>U: Return without posting this task else Gate permits the captured scope L-->>S: Ready S->>D: Reset dependency only if its revision is unchanged D-->>S: Guarded restoration callback when reset occurred S->>A: POST body with client submission ID alt Acknowledgement received A-->>S: Accepted task and conversation identities S->>S: Mark acceptance and discard pending retry ID S->>D: Remember prompt and consume matching original-scope draft S->>S: Check navigation before updating current views S-->>U: Adopt accepted conversation and reconcile task state else Request fails before acknowledgement A--xS: Rejection or uncertain delivery S->>S: Discard identity for definite failure, retain it otherwise S->>D: Restore only the still-owned dependency selection S-->>U: Present failure in the current scope end end

Loading the conversation view module is not conversation creation. A new task can still be sent without a conversation ID, and the accepted server response supplies the new conversation identity. The provisional card is mounted after the view module loads and before the agreement check completes. A gate refusal can mark that provisional submission rejected without sending it.

Rejected and unconfirmed submissions retain the full structured error in a visible conversation card, independently of the runtime-issues display preference. The mobile notice also offers Details for recovery steps and the error reference. Field validation lists show the field and requirement, without copying submitted values. Invalid JSON responses remain failures; they cannot be treated as successful empty acknowledgements. These notices last for the page view and do not create a server task-history record.

Before POST, dependency reset occurs only if the revision still equals the one captured at the start. A newer selection therefore remains visible even though the body retains the originally captured dependency. On failure the restoration closure also checks conversation, revision and an empty current selection. See dependency restoration.

The mobile pending map stores retry IDs, not retained request bodies. Each new submit reconstructs a body from current composer state. An identical serialized body reuses its pending ID; changing captured intent can produce a new identity. This differs from the desktop controller's retained pending body. Neither map survives a page reload, and neither is the durable server queue.

An error before POST is definite. After POST begins, HTTP 4xx is also classified as definite; other failures retain the pending ID. A composer_state_changed error requests a refresh. Once the acknowledgement arrives, later UI failures produce “Task accepted” feedback and do not revoke acceptance or submit again.

Accepted text is remembered for completion. Matching pending/saved text is consumed under its original conversation scope, and that scope's capability draft is cleared. The current textarea is cleared only if it still equals the submitted text. After the navigation check, the shell adopts the accepted conversation, clears the resource editor, removes submitted attachment IDs and reconciles state. Newer text is retained; these text checks are not a promise that every resource or policy draft survives acceptance. The accepted request ID may arrive later through canonical reconciliation.

Queue sheet reads and mutations

Opening the sheet captures conversation and navigation generation. It uses the shell's cached canonical lane when present; otherwise it reads a compact lane, including the selected dependency query, and adapts indexed task IDs through laneView. A late initial response is ignored if navigation changed or its sheet body was removed. No extra update stream or polling timer is created.

sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant Q as Mobile queue sheet participant O as Overlay owner participant R as Canonical snapshot owner participant A as Task and lane APIs U->>Q: Open queued messages Q->>O: Open or replace the single sheet alt Canonical lane is cached Q->>Q: Use current page lane else No cached lane Q->>A: GET compact lane and selected dependency A-->>Q: Indexed lane Q->>Q: Check generation and connected body, adapt task order end Q->>Q: Render queue rows and install owned laneChanged callback R-->>Q: Later lane projection Q->>Q: Update dependency text and non-editing Start controls only U->>Q: Edit, remove, reorder, steer or explicitly start Q->>A: Send mutation with the required observed version alt Mutation accepted A-->>Q: Result Q->>R: Refresh canonical conversation state R-->>Q: Current lane Q->>O: Replace sheet only if original generation and body still match else Mutation rejected or transport fails A--xQ: Error Q-->>U: Button owner displays error and releases disabled state end U->>O: Close or replace sheet O->>Q: Invoke close callback Q->>Q: Remove callback only if it is still this sheet's callback

The open sheet lists queued tasks, the active-task status and any lane block reason. Run next is offered only when the server advertises it. Dependency-blocked queued tasks gain Start task; the button stores the latest observed version in its dataset. Server execution slots still apply.

Edit loads full task detail before replacing a connected row with a textarea. The field has a 24,000-character maximum and shared history completion. Save PATCHes its text; server validation handles invalid content. There is no separate Cancel edit button in this sheet: closing/reopening discards an unsaved row editor. Remove deletes queued intent. Move up submits the whole reordered queued-ID list with the captured lane version; mobile does not expose a separate Move down button.

When an active task exists, rows without explicit dependencies offer both steering actions. The mobile sheet delegates compatibility and status validation to the server rather than performing the desktop envelope comparison. Gentle steering sends steering_mode: after_response.

Each button disables itself while its action runs, then restores itself. This is per-button serialization, not a lock across the whole sheet. A successful ordinary mutation refreshes canonical state and reopens the sheet only while the original generation and body still match. API failures propagate to the button's notice handler; they do not automatically replace the sheet. Clear queued messages checks the current conversation, deletes its queued intent, refreshes and reopens only if that conversation is still selected. It does not cancel the active task.

Live update and close boundaries

hooks.laneChanged updates dependency explanations for existing rows and adds, removes or refreshes Start controls when those rows are not being edited. It does not rebuild the list, reorder rows, replace prompt text or add/remove task rows. The full inventory is refreshed on a full reopen, including reopening after a successful action. An old reorder button can therefore carry an older observed version; the server decides whether to accept it. This deliberately preserves text and focus while a row editor is open.

The callback ignores a different conversation/generation or disconnected body. The close callback removes hooks.laneChanged only when it still points to this sheet's callback, so replacement cleanup cannot remove a successor's owner. Closing a sheet does not abort HTTP transport, undo an accepted mutation or stop server task execution. Shared overlay code owns focus, modal containment, browser Back and the close animation.

Evidence and scope

The three dedicated submission-options, dependency-selector and queue-sheet modules were reviewed in full. Submission/snapshot callbacks, transport/button helpers and overlay mounting/cleanup were reviewed at the stated boundaries. Theme and tooltip work remains outside this review. Relevant browser fixtures include dependency selection and the dedicated mobile queue scenarios. They use local state and mocked APIs. Results and any baseline failures are recorded in the review ledger; they do not certify live Gateway/model execution or physical mobile devices.
